title: Attorney General Ellison holds CVS accountable for submitting false Medicaid claims related to insulin pens
supports: Minnesota joined a $36.5 million national settlement resolving allegations that CVS submitted false claims to government health programs relating to insulin-pen dispensing.

The Minnesota Attorney General states CVS will pay more than $850,000 attributable to conduct in Minnesota, including more than $400,000 in direct restitution to Minnesota's Medical Assistance program.
The allegations cover 2010 through 2020 and involve over-dispensing insulin pens, under-reporting days of supply, and premature refill claims.
The release states CVS accepted responsibility for specified conduct as part of the settlement.

money.scope: direct restitution to Minnesota Medical Assistance
money.notes: Settlement restitution, not a criminal restitution order.

important_qualifications: This is a civil settlement resolving allegations; do not describe it as a criminal conviction.
The Minnesota-attributable settlement amount and direct Medicaid restitution are nested/overlapping figures and must not be added together.
This recovery should remain separate from the MFCU annual $24M recovery statistic unless overlap is resolved.
